To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Immuno-suppression (immunoprotetion) in experimental autoimmuneencephalomyelitis is mediated by suppressor T lymphocyte cells, 2) Suppression is antigen specific, 3) Suppressor cells are present in spleens of mice immunized for EAA, 4) Suppression is not mediated by cells of non-lymphoid origin, 5) Suppression is mediated by T cells bearing the Thy-1 antigen.
suppressor cells can be induced in experimental autoimmune encehphalomyelitis and can inhibit the disease.
suppressor T cells can inhibit the induction and expression of experimental autoimmune encephalo-myelitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunobiology of experimental allergic encephalomyetitis (EAE), a disease which resembles multiple sclerosis (MS) in man.
experimental autoimmune encephalo-myelitis (EAM), an animal disease that is analogous to multiple sclerosis (MS), a human demyelinating disease.
the mechanisms by which T lymphocytes suppress the development and expression of autoimmune diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the suppressive activity is due to a suppressor T cell, which can be demonstrated in the spleen and bone marrow, and that the suppressor T cell is Thy-1 positive.

the immunoprotection against experimental autoimmune encephalytomyelitis in the mouse is mediated by the recruitment of a specific suppressor T cell which is Thy-1 positive and is specific for the relevant antigen, basic protein.
the suppressor T cells are the most important cells in the immune response, because they are able to suppress both the effector T cells and the antigen presenting cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the suppressor cells are T lymphocytes and that they act in two ways: they inhibit the development of effector cells after antigenic challenge, and they block the damaging effects of the effector cells on the central nervous system.
suppressor T cells are the major mediators of immunosuppression in EAE.
the immune system is capable of generating suppressor T cells that can protect against the induction of autoimmune disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can induce tolerance in the CNS by using the suppressor cells to inhibit the development of effector cells and their ability to damage the CNS.

we were able to demonstrate that the adoptively transferred suppressor cells were able to prevent the development of EAE in the recipient mouse, as well as to block the effector function in mice already immunized for EEA.
the suppression of EAE in mice is due to suppressor T cells, which are recruited by the antigenic stimulation of the mice.
